title: Ensure Cloud Object Storage buckets are not publicly accessible
description: COS public access is granted through policies on the account's Public Access group. That group must have no cloud-object-storage policies (passes if the group does not exist). Read-only ibmcloud CLI calls using the current CLI session and targeted region (ibmcloud login, or IBMCLOUD_API_KEY); JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI, plugin or session fails the check.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - Storage - Cloud Object Storage public access disabled (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
grp=$(ibmcloud iam access-groups --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
if ! printf '%s\n' "$grp" | grep -q '"Public Access"'; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi
out=$(ibmcloud iam access-group-policies "Public Access" --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '"cloud-object-storage"' || true)
[ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Remove the cloud-object-storage policies from the Public Access group (ibmcloud iam access-group-policy-delete "Public Access" <policy-id>) and disable public access in the COS console.

title: Ensure no owner account API key exists
description: API keys by definition allow access to your account and resources in your account. The API key authenticates the identity and allows all access assigned to the identity for which it was created, therefore an API key created by user with administrative privileges has administrative level access to resources in the account. In accordance with the practice of granting least privilege, API keys should not be created by an account owner because of the level of privilege automatically granted to account-owner created API keys.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure no owner account API key exists

audit.command: To check for the existence of an API key created by an administrative user, complete the following steps. 1. Login as any administrative user at cloud.ibm.com 2. Click Manage, Access (IAM) 3. Click API keys 4. Check for any API keys that appear under the My IBM Cloud API keys view

remediation.command: To delete an API key, complete the following steps: 1. Login as the administrative user at cloud.ibm.com 2. In the console, go to Manage, Access (IAM) 3. Click on API keys 4. Identify the row of the API key that you want to delete and select Delete from the Actions List of actions icon menu (found on the right hand side of the row). 5. Then, confirm the deletion by clicking Delete. 6. If you have scenarios where you need a higher level of access, then you should setup a Trusted Profile with these privileges and use it with a less privileged identity

title: Ensure Context-Based Restrictions are implemented to enforce secure, conditional access to critical resources based on network location, IP range, or identity attributes
description: IBM Cloud Context-Based Restrictions are a security feature that allows administrators to control access to cloud resources based on the context of the request, such as the IP address the request is made from, not just the identity of the user or service. IBM Cloud's Context-Based Restrictions (CBRs) provide an essential layer of defense by enforcing access conditions based on network location or type of endpoint, not just IAM roles. This means even if a user has the correct permissions, their request can be blocked if it originates from an untrusted context. By implementing CBRs, organizations can reduce the risk of unauthorized access, enforce compliance policies, and protect critical services like Cloud Object Storage, Key Protect, and Secrets Manager. In short, CBRs help turn identity-based access into context-aware security, which is vital in today’s hybrid and distributed enviro...
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.12 Ensure Context-Based Restrictions are implemented to enforce secure, conditional access to critical resources based on network location, IP range, or identity attributes

audit.command: To check if you have a Context-Based Restriction (CBR) set in IBM Cloud, follow these steps: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud Console: 2. Navigate to IAM, Context-based restrictions in the left-hand menu 3. Under the Rules tab, you'll see a list of all active CBR rules in your account. Each rule will show: o The network zone it applies to (e.g., IP ranges, VPCs) o The target service or resource (e.g., Cloud Object Storage, Key Protect) o The action (allow or deny) o Any conditions or exceptions 4. You can click on each rule to view its details, including which users or services it affects and when it was last modified. 5. If no rules are listed, then no CBRs are currently enforced in your account.

remediation.command: To create new trusted profile, complete the following steps: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud Console: 2. Navigate to Manage, Context-based restrictions, then select Network zones from the left navigation menu. 3. click Create and define the network zone(s) you want to allow access from, using allowed or denied IP addresses, subnets, or ranges, VPCs, and IBM Cloud services. 4. Select Rules from the left navigation menu 5. Click Create and select the service, APIs, and resources you want the rule to apply to, select the context including the zone you defined, and specify whether to enable or report on this rule.

title: Ensure IAM Does Not Allow Public Access to Cloud Services
description: IBM Cloud features the capability for users with specific access roles to create access policies that allow all users (authenticated and non-authenticated) to access resources in the account. This “all users” access in turn ends up in public (including non- authenticated) access to resources. Determine if this capability is required by your organization and disable if not required. Some customer use cases require that certain files or data are made available for all users to access, both authenticated and non-authenticated. Even if the public access setting is enabled, resources in your account are not publicly accessible unless an administrator level user has explicitly created a policy to create public access for a resource. As a best practice, if this capability is not required by your organization, it must be disabled to prevent unintentional misuse.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.18 Ensure IAM Does Not Allow Public Access to Cloud Services

audit.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to IBM Cloud at https://cloud.ibm.com. 2. From the Menu bar, click Manage, Access (IAM). 3. Click Settings. 4. If the Public access group setting is enabled, proceed to the Access groups page by clicking Access Groups. 7. From the list of Access Groups, select Public Access by clicking on the Access Group name. 8. Ensure that there are no access policies present for services in the list of access policies.

remediation.command: Using Console: To disable the Public Access Group: 1. Log in to IBM Cloud at https://cloud.ibm.com. 2. From the Menu bar, click Manage, Access (IAM). 3. In the public access section of IAM Settings, observe the Public access group setting. 5. If the Public access group setting is disabled, IAM is not providing public access. 6. If the Public access group setting is enabled, proceed to the Access groups page by clicking Access Groups. 7. From the list of Access Groups, select Public Access by clicking on the Access Group name. 8. Ensure that there are no access policies present in the list of access policies. 9. To delete an access policy, click on the action menu icon for the access policy and click Remove.

title: Ensure Public (anonymous) Access to IBM Cloud Object Storage buckets is Disabled
description: You can disable public (anonymous) access to IBM Cloud Object Storage buckets. Buckets might have to hold open data sets for academic, research, or image repositories that are used by web applications and content delivery networks. You can make these buckets publicly accessible by using the Public Access group. But when buckets contain non-public data (e.g., restricted, internal, confidential or sensitive data), it is important to have public access disabled. To disable the public access, a previously defined access policy must be removed. By default, public access to Cloud Object Storage buckets is disabled. If an access policy is defined that allows public access, you can disable the policy by using the console.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.1.5 Ensure Public (anonymous) Access to IBM Cloud Object Storage buckets is Disabled

audit.command: To check if an access policy exists for a Cloud Object Storage bucket, you can list the access policies for the Public Access group. Using Console: 1. Check the list of access polices to see if one exists for the relevant Cloud Object Storage bucket.

remediation.command: To disable public access for buckets, complete the following steps: Using Console: 1. Log in to IBM Cloud at https://cloud.ibm.com. 2. Find the policy that corresponds to the bucket that you want to return to enforced access control. 6. From the list of actions, select Remove. 7. Confirm that you want to remove the policy.

title: Ensure IBM Cloud® File Storage for Virtual Private Cloud is encrypted with provider managed keys
description: By default, IBM Cloud® File Storage for Virtual Private Cloud provides provider- managed encryption for all data. For enhanced security, customers can bring their own encryption keys and manage them through IBM Key Management Services – Key Protect or Hyper Protect Crypto Services (HPCS). With provider-managed keys, the file service manages encryption at rest by default with no additional configuration needed by the customer. With provider managed encryption, the service manages the root encryption keys on behalf of the customer.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.2.2.1 Ensure IBM Cloud® File Storage for Virtual Private Cloud is encrypted with provider managed keys

audit.command: You can use the IBM® Cloud File Storage for Virtual Private Cloud configuration properties to verify whether a file share is enabled with provider managed encryption. From the IBM Cloud Console, Navigate to your file share resource: 1. In the IBM Cloud console, go to Menu icon, VPC Infrastructure, Storage, File Storage Shares. A list of all file shares is displays. 2. For each of the shares listed, ensure the encryption field specifies Provider Managed.

remediation.command: You will not be able to change the encryption option once data is already written to a File Share. In order to change your encryption setting you will need to create a new File Share, set it to use your desired encryption setting and then upload/copy the existing data to this new share.

title: Ensure IBM Cloud Databases disk encryption is enabled with customer managed keys
description: IBM Cloud Databases provides automatic encryption at rest when provisioning the service. It is not an option to deploy a database service without encryption at rest. However, using the service's integration with IBM Key Protect, customers can bring their own encryption key at the time of database provisioning. Furthermore, IBM Cloud Databases backups are also encrypted by default. Before any UI or CLI commands. Follow the authorization instructions between the HSM and Database service. 1. Open your IBM Cloud dashboard. 2. From the menu bar, click Manage, Access (IAM). 3. In the side navigation, click Authorizations. 4. Click Create. 5. In the Source service menu, select the service of the deployment. For example, Databases for PostgreSQL or Messages for RabbitMQ 6. In the Source service instance menu, select All instances. 7. In the Target service menu, select Key Protect. 8. Select o...

audit.command: Using Console: 1. Log on to your IBM Cloud account 2. Go to the Menu icon, Resource List to access your list of account resources 3. Click the Database service you are interested in to open the service dashboard. 4. Ensure you are on the Manage page in the left pane. 5. You should be on the Overview tab. Scroll down to the security section. 6. The security section will show an Encryption Key section under Disks. If the value shown is Automatic Key this means the deployment does not have a customer-managed encryption key through IBM Key Protect Using CLI: 1. At a minimum, have the Viewer role for the IBM Cloud Databases deployment. 2. Run ibmcloud cdb deployment-about <CRN> [--all] [--json] This will return the Encryption Key Status, if the deployment is created with a customer- managed encryption key, the key CRN will display here.

remediation.command: There is no zero-downtime remediation procedure . Customer must restore a backup with a new encryption key or create a net new database instance with Bring Your Own Key enabled. To restore a backup with a new encryption key: 1. Ensure you have the Viewer Privileges on the IBM Cloud Databases deployment to read a backup file and X privileges on IBM Cloud platform to create a resource 2. Ensure you have service to service authorization set up between IBM Cloud Databases and IBM Key Protect, directions for granting this access can be found here 3. Be sure to replace SERVICE_INSTANCE_NAME and KEY PROTECT KEY CRN with a new service instance name and your desired Key Protect key CRN respectively before running this command. For more information, please view our documentation. ibmcloud resource service-instance-create SERVICE_INSTANCE_NAME databases- for-postgresql standard us-south -p '{"backup_id":"xyz-inital- backup","disk_encryption_key_crn":"DISK_ENCRYPTION_KEY_CRN"}' 4. This will create a new database instance from backup with the requested customer managed encryption key.

Context-based restrictions give account owners and administrators the ability to define and enforce access restrictions for resources based on a rule's criteria. The criteria include the network location of access requests, the endpoint type from where the request is sent, the multifactor authentication level of an identity, and sometimes the API that the request tries to access.

title: Ensure all data stores are encrypted in the IBM Cloud®
description: When you provision any data services in the IBM Cloud, such as Cloud Object Storage, Databases such as PostGreSQL, MongoDB, database for ElasticSearch, ETCD, backups created for any data store, and data volumes for compute etc., you want to encrypt the data-at-rest with your root key that you created in Key Protect key management service. You can use Bring Your Own Key (CRK) or provider key to enable encryption of your data-at-rest in data store associated with any of the services in the IBM Cloud that is integrated with the Key Protect Service. By encrypting your data with your own root key or service provided root key, you are protecting your data from unwanted access to your data. Even if the data is accessed, attacker cannot view the data as the encryption key is not stored with the data

title: Ensure the Default Network Security Group of Every Workspace Restricts All Traffic
description: It is recommended that the default security group for every workspace restricts all inbound (ingress) traffic, to enforce a least-privilege security posture and reduce unintended exposure of PowerVS resources. Starting with a default security group configuration that restricts all inbound (ingress) traffic reduces the chance of exposing PowerVS resources to unintended risks.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 9.1 Ensure the Default Network Security Group of Every Workspace Restricts All Traffic

audit.command: Perform the following tasks to determine if the account is configured as prescribed: Using Console: 1. Login to the IBM Cloud Portal at https://cloud.ibm.com and select Power Virtual Server user interface. 2. In the navigation panel, click Workspaces, then for each workspace that contains Network Security Groups, open the Workspace details page. 3. From the workspace details page, click view virtual servers. 4. In the left navigation panel, expand Networking and then select Network Security Groups. 5. For the default security group, perform the following: a. Ensure no rule exists that allows inbound (ingress) traffic flow to the Virtual Servers in the group.

remediation.command: Using Console: 1. Login to the IBM Cloud Portal at https://cloud.ibm.com and select Power Virtual Server user interface. 2. From the workspace details page, click view virtual servers. 4. In the left navigation panel, expand Networking and then select Network Security Groups. 5. For the default security group, perform the following: a. Identify the rule that allows inbound (ingress) traffic flows. b. Remove the rule.

title: Ensure multi-factor authentication is enabled for all users in the account
description: Account-level MFA forces a second factor for every login. The account setting mfa must not be NONE / NONE_NO_ROPC (TOTP4ALL or a LEVEL setting covers federated users as well). Read-only ibmcloud CLI calls using the current CLI session and targeted region (ibmcloud login, or IBMCLOUD_API_KEY); JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI, plugin or session fails the check.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - Identity and Access Management - account-level MFA (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: ibmcloud iam account-settings-update --mfa TOTP4ALL (or LEVEL1-3 for IBMid/App ID users), or Manage > Access (IAM) > Settings > Authentication.

title: Ensure Activity Tracker event routing is configured
description: Activity Tracker Event Routing sends account audit events to a durable target (Cloud Logs, COS, Event Streams). At least one route with target_ids must exist (requires the atracker plugin). Read-only ibmcloud CLI calls using the current CLI session and targeted region (ibmcloud login, or IBMCLOUD_API_KEY); JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI, plugin or session fails the check.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - Logging and Monitoring - Activity Tracker event routing (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
out=$(ibmcloud atracker route ls --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
n=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '"target_ids"' || true)
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: ibmcloud atracker target create --name <t> --type cloud_object_storage|cloud_logs ... then ibmcloud atracker route create --name <r> --rules '[{"locations":["*","global"],"target_ids":["<target-id>"]}]'.

title: Ensure no VPC security groups allow inbound 0.0.0.0/0 to port 22 or 3389
description: SSH and RDP open to the Internet are brute-forced continuously. In the targeted region, no inbound rule of any VPC security group may allow remote 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to tcp 22/3389 or all protocols (requires the vpc-infrastructure plugin). Read-only ibmcloud CLI calls using the current CLI session and targeted region (ibmcloud login, or IBMCLOUD_API_KEY); JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI, plugin or session fails the check.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - Networking - VPC security groups restrict SSH/RDP from 0.0.0.0/0 (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: ibmcloud is security-group-rule-delete <sg> <rule> (or security-group-rule-update --remote <admin-cidr>) for the offending rules; use a bastion / VPN for administration.

title: Monitor account owner for frequent, unexpected, or unauthorized logins
description: Monitor login activity of the account owner to prevent unauthorized usage of the privileged account. The owner of an IBM Cloud account by default has administrative privileges across the account. There may be other users also assigned administrative privileges to the account. To prevent unauthorized or unintended usage, login credentials should never be shared and users in an organization should be granted least privilege to complete their required tasks. To manage the account, administrators are granted permissions to manage services and Cloud resources. Therefore, access by the account owner to the account to run tasks should be minimum. By monitoring the number of times that the account owner and administrative users log in to the account, you can: - Monitor administrative access to the IBM Cloud account - Identify abnormal behavior - Enforce that administrators and operators of th...
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.1 Monitor account owner for frequent, unexpected, or unauthorized logins

audit.command: Before you can monitor and manage IBM event data with IBM Cloud Logs, you must provision an instance of the IBM Cloud Logs service. Refer to the IBM Cloud Logs documentation to provision and start using an instance of IBM Cloud Logs https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/cloud-logs?topic=cloud-logs-getting-started.

remediation.command: Complete the following steps to monitor how many times an account owner logs in to the account: First, you need to identify the email of the account owner. 1. In the Cloud UI, go to Manage, Access (IAM), then select Users. 2. Identify the users identified with administrator privileges. 3. Select the account owner. Then, click Details. 4. Copy the email address of the account owner. Launch the Activity Tracker instance in Frankfurt. This is the instance where login security events are collected in the account. In the Views section, select the Everything view. Then, enter the following query in the search bar: (action login) AND initiator.name:<email address> Replace with the account owner's email address. The view now reports all the login actions that are reported for the account owner. Next, you can define an alert on the view to get a notification when N number of events are received within a 24 hour period. The value of N depends on how you operate your cloud. You can start with a default value of 25 and increase or decrease depending on the tasks that the account administrator can perform in the account.

title: Ensure API keys unused for 180 days are detected and optionally disabled
description: Monitor API key usage in your account and search for API keys that are unused or used infrequently. If an API key is unused for long period in your account, it must be suspended or disabled as a security best practice. All API keys, even those that are used infrequently, must be rotated periodically. To reduce the likelihood of accidental exposure or leaking, monitoring for infrequently used API keys can indicate that an API key can be suspended and even deleted, if there is no anticipated future usage.

remediation.command: On the Inactive Identities report under API keys tab, review and remove the API keys no longer in use. To delete inactive identities that are no longer in use for over 180 days, click the Actions icon, Remove

title: Ensure API keys are rotated every 90 days
description: Replace production API keys with new API keys regularly, every 90 days for example, as a best practice to secure your account. API key rotation can help reduce the impact to your organization if an API key becomes exposed or compromised. If you suspect that a key might have been leaked or compromised, the key must be rotated out of production and deleted.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure API keys are rotated every 90 days

title: Restrict user API key creation and service ID creation in the account via IAM roles
description: Use IAM settings to restrict user API key creation and service ID (and related API key) creation in the account. API keys authenticate IBM Cloud identities. Service IDs are intended to be used by applications and other programmatic entities, and so they persist in an account even after users who created them or had access to them have been deleted. Crea...
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.4 Restrict user API key creation and service ID creation in the account via IAM roles

title: Ensure Trusted Profiles are used in place of ServiceIDs wherever feasible
description: IBM Cloud trusted profiles are used to securely manage identity and access for applications running on IBM Cloud without relying on static credentials like API keys. One use of Trusted Profiles is to allow an application running on an IBM Cloud compute resource to assume the Trusted Profile and its access based on the identity of the compute resource where it is running, eliminating the need for the application to store and manage an API key. Trusted Profiles are preferred over ServiceIDs because they offer a more secure, scalable, and maintainable approach to identity and access management. Unlike ServiceIDs, which are static and tied to specific credentials, Trusted Profiles leverage the built-in identities of compute resources to assign least privilege access to applications running on those compute resources. They reduce the risk of credential sprawl and simplify auditing and comp...

title: Ensure IAM users with the same level of access are members of access groups and IAM policies are assigned only to access groups or Trusted Profiles

title: Ensure Minimal Number of Users are Granted Administrative Privileges
description: Comply with the principle of granting least privilege by using Access Groups or Trusted Profiles to manage admin privileges and by avoiding the use of broadly scoped access policies. The principle of granting least privilege mandates that a user must only be given access to the resources that are required to complete their task. This task can be hard to maintain when managing large numbers of users. Instead of assigning administrative privileges to individual users, create Access Groups with administrative privileges and add or remove users from these Access Groups as needed. Additionally, instead of using the Platform Administrator role for all Platform Services or all IAM-enabled services, IBM Cloud users can grant access to specific resources and account management services to better comply with the principle of granting least privilege.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.16 Ensure Minimal Number of Users are Granted Administrative Privileges

audit.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to IBM Cloud at https://cloud.ibm.com. 2. From the Menu bar, click Manage, Access(IAM). 3. Click Users and select a User by clicking on the User name. 4. Click on the Access Policies tab. View the access policies assigned to the User to verify if that User has Administrator Role assigned. 5. Review Access Groups and Trusted Profiles to determine which grant Administrator privileges. 6. For Access Groups and Trusted Profiles that grant Administrator. privileges, review which users are members of the Access Groups or allowed to assume the Trusted Profiles. 7. Verify that all users who have Administrator privileges have a legitimate need for those privileges.

remediation.command: Using Console: To remove excessive number of Users with Administrative privileges, follow the following steps. 1. Log in to IBM Cloud at https://cloud.ibm.com. 2. If there are users who have Administrator privileges but do not have a legitimate need for them, remove the user’s access policy or remove the user from the Access Group or Trusted. Profile. Alternatively you may remove the user from the account.

title: Ensure Cloud Object Storage encryption is done with customer managed keys

audit.command: Using API/CLI: Use of Server-Side Encryption with Customer-Provided Keys (SSE-C) can be validated by the following steps: Note: Ensure that you have completed the configuration setup to use the CLI by following the guidelines on the Using the AWS CLI page 1. title: Ensure Cloud Object Storage Encryption is set to On with BYOK

title: Ensure Key Protect root keys have a rotation policy
description: Rotation policies regularly re-wrap data encryption keys with new root key material. Every root (non-extractable) key in every Key Protect instance must have a rotation policy with interval_month (requires the kp plugin; keys are queried in the targeted region). Read-only ibmcloud CLI calls using the current CLI session and targeted region (ibmcloud login, or IBMCLOUD_API_KEY); JSON output is parsed with grep/sed/awk. A missing CLI, plugin or session fails the check.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - Storage - Key Protect root key rotation (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
inst=$(ibmcloud resource service-instances --service-name kms --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
bad=0
for g in $(printf '%s\n' "$inst" | awk '{ o = gsub(/\{/, "{"); c = gsub(/\}/, "}") } d == 1 && /"guid"[[:space:]]*:/ { s = $0; sub(/^[^:]*:[[:space:]]*"/, "", s); sub(/".*/, "", s); print s } { d += o - c }'); do
  ks=$(ibmcloud kp keys -i "$g" --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  ids=$(printf '%s\n' "$ks" | awk '{ o = gsub(/\{/, "{"); c = gsub(/\}/, "}") } d == 0 && o > 0 { id = ""; ex = "" } d == 1 && /"id"[[:space:]]*:/ { id = $0; sub(/^[^:]*:[[:space:]]*"/, "", id); sub(/".*/, "", id) } d == 1 && /"extractable"[[:space:]]*:/ { ex = $0 } { d += o - c } d == 0 && c > 0 && ex ~ /false/ { print id }')
  for k in $ids; do
    p=$(ibmcloud kp key policies "$k" -i "$g" --output json 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    printf '%s\n' "$p" | grep -q '"interval_month"' || { echo "no rotation policy: $g $k"; bad=1; }
  done
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: ibmcloud kp key policy-update rotation <key-id> -i <instance-id> --monthly-interval 12 (or shorter); alternatively set an instance-level rotation policy (ibmcloud kp instance policy-update rotation).

By default, logs are generated and written locally for all the following IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service cluster components: worker nodes, containers, applications, persistent storage, Ingress application load balancer, Kubernetes API, and the kube- system namespace. IBM Cloud Logs supports integration with common workload environments on IBM Cloud - including IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service - and provides observability services so you can view, analyze, and alert on activity tracking events and logging activity. A logging agent collects logs with the extension *.log and extensionless files that are stored in the /var/log/containers directory of your pod from all namespaces, including kube-system. audit.command: From Console: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud console. 2. To view a list of your clusters, go to Menu, Containers, Clusters. 3. From the Clusters page, select your cluster. 4. Select the Overview tab 5. Under Integrations, the Logging item should have a button to Launch the IBM Cloud Log dashboard. If instead the button is labelled Connect, then logging is not enabled. From Command Line: 1. Check that a daemonset logs-agent exists in the namespace ibm-observe. kubectl get ds -n ibm-observe 2. Verify the log agents are started. kubectl -n ibm-observe get ds logs-agent 3. Verify that a logs-agent pod is ready for each node in your cluster. kubectl get pods -n ibm-observe -o wide 4. Optionally: view the logs of a pod. kubectl logs <POD_NAME>> -n ibm-observe

title: Ensure notification service is enabled in the IBM Cloud Secrets Manager to notify life cycle events
description: Secrets stored in the Secrets Manager go through life-cycle changes, as an administrator of your Secrets Manager instance, you may want to notify your users, applications through available delivery channels such as email, SMS etc., or through event-driven programming using webhooks. Ensuring all secrets life cycle management is handled on-time to ensure users are not locked out and applications run without disruptions.
reference: CIS IBM Cloud Foundations Benchmark v2.0.0 - 8.2.3 Ensure notification service is enabled in the IBM Cloud Secrets Manager to notify life cycle events

audit.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud® console. 2. Go to Menu, Resource List to view a list of your resources. 3. Click on Security and click on the Secrets Manager instance that you want to use 4. Click on Settings on the left-hand panel to check if event notification is configured for the instance.

remediation.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud® console. 2. Go to Menu, Resource List to view a list of your resources. 3. Click on Security and click on the Secrets Manager instance that you want to use 4. In the Secrets Manager navigation, click Settings. 5. In the Event Notifications section and click Connect. 6. In the side panel, review the source details for the connection. 7. Select the resource group and Event Notifications service instance that you want to connect. 8. To confirm the connection, click `Connect'. 9. A success message is displayed to indicate that Secrets Manager is now connected to Event Notifications. If an IAM authorization between Secrets Manager and Event Notifications doesn't exist in your account, a dialog is displayed. Follow the prompts to grant access between the services. 1. To grant access between Secrets Manager and Event Notifications, click Authorize. 2. In the side panel, select Event Notifications as the target service. 3. From the list of instances, select the Event Notifications service instance that you want to authorize. 4. Select the Event Source Manager role. 5. Click Review. 6. Click Assign.

title: Ensure secrets stored in the IBM Cloud® Secrets Manager are rotated periodically
description: As you use Secrets Manager to design your secrets management strategy, consider how often you want to rotate your secrets based on the internal guidelines for your organization. Determine ahead of time which users or service IDs require access to rotate secrets, and how those secrets can be rotated to avoid interruptions to your applications. By scheduling automatic rotation of secrets at regular intervals, you reduce the likelihood of compromised credentials. When it's time to rotate the secret based on the rotation interval that you specify, Secrets Manager automatically creates a new version of your secret. You can safely delete old version of the secrets only after their newest versions are fully deployed to your applications. audit.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud® console. 2. Go to Menu, Resource List to view a list of your resources. 3. Click on Security and click on the Secrets Manager instance that you want to view 4. In the Secrets table, click the Actions menu to open a list of options for your secret 5. To view the secret value, click View Secret 6. Click Confirm after you ensure that you are in a safe environment 7. To retrieve a secret’s details such as rotation interval or state; In the Secrets table, click the Actions menu, to open a list of options for your secret 8. To view the secret value, click Details.

remediation.command: Using Console: 1. Log in to the IBM Cloud® console. 2. Go to Menu, Resource List to view a list of your resources. 3. Click on Security and click on the Secrets Manager instance that you want to use 4. If you're adding a secret, enable the rotation option. 5. If you're editing an existing secret, enable automatic rotation by updating its details. 6. In the Secrets table, view a list of your existing secrets. 7. In the row for the secret that you want to edit, click the Actions menu, Edit details 8. Use the Automatic rotation option to enable or disable automatic rotation for the secret.
